name: Short Bowel Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Short Bowel Syndrome

criteria.description: History of extensive small intestine resection resulting in less than 200 cm of functional small bowel
Evidence of malabsorption including nutrient deficiencies and steatorrhea
Dependence on parenteral nutrition for maintenance of hydration and nutrition

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of history of extensive small bowel resection with clinical and laboratory evidence of malabsorption
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by imaging and nutritional assessment

occasional.symptomName: Vitamin and mineral deficiencies (e.g., vitamin B12, iron, calcium)

rare.notes: Though hepatic is not in the valid body systems, this is a known complication; omitted from systemsAffected

rare.symptomName: Osteomalacia due to vitamin D deficiency

laboratory: Low serum levels of vitamins (B12, A, D, E, K)
Anemia due to iron or B12 deficiency
imaging: Abdominal CT or MRI showing shortened small intestine
Small bowel follow-through demonstrating reduced length and dilated segments
other: Evidence of malabsorption on stool studies (e.g., increased fecal fat)

distinguishingFeatures: Histologic villous atrophy without history of bowel resection
Imaging showing pancreatic calcifications or ductal changes

redFlags: Signs of liver failure or cholestasis
references: O'Keefe SJ. Short bowel syndrome: pathophysiology and clinical management. J Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2006.
Pironi L, et al. ESPEN guidelines on chronic intestinal failure in adults. Clin Nutr. 2018.
Nightingale JMD. Intestinal failure. Best Pract Res Clin Gastroenterol. 2006.
